method: I opened each of the five JPEG scans (s39–s43) directly with the Read image tool, at 1208x2000 display resolution from 1368x2264 originals. I did not run OCR, look at any first-reader transcription, or check other editions or standard liturgical texts. I read the pages in scan order, line by line. I kept the source's punctuation, maqaf, line-level structure and visible pointing as best the resolution allowed. Where a mark was unclear, I transcribed my best reading and listed it under uncertainties instead of correcting it to a standard text. The Hebrew linkage words at the start of English paragraphs are in linkage_cue, not in the English text. I rejoined English words split by end-of-line hyphens and noted each one.

blocks.text: סֵדֶר עֲטִיפַת הַטַּלִּית.
uncertainties: There is a small mark at the right of the ע in עֲטִיפַת, possibly a meteg/ga'ya or decorative mark. I recorded only the hataf-patah.

blocks.text: Before draping oneself in the טלית the following is said:

הִנְנִי מִתְעַטֵּף בְּטַלִּית שֶׁל־צִיצִת כְּדֵי לְקַיֵּם מִצְוַת בּוֹרְאִי כַּכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה וְעָשׂוּ לָהֶם צִיצִת עַל־כַּנְפֵי בִגְדֵיהֶם לְדֹרֹתָם. וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֲנִי מִתְכַּסֶּה בְטַלִּית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כֵּן תִּזְכֶּה נִשְׁמָתִי לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּטַלִּית נָאָה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּגַן עֵדֶן, אָמֵן:
uncertainties: The first letter of בַּתּוֹרָה could be ב or כ (כַּתּוֹרָה). I read ב.
I can't tell whether בִגְדֵיהֶם (line-initial) has a dagesh in the ב.
The punctuation between עֵדֶן and אָמֵן looks like a comma, not a period.
I can't confirm the dagesh in בְטַלִּית before בָּעוֹלָם; it looks absent.

blocks.text: Then this ברכה is recited while standing:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ לְהִתְעַטֵּף בַּצִּיצִת:
uncertainties: The divine name is printed as two yods with pointing (יְיָ); I can't resolve the exact vowel marks at this resolution.

blocks.text: One then drapes oneself in the טלית and says:

מַה־יָּקָר חַסְדְּךָ אֱלֹהִים וּבְנֵי אָדָם בְּצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ יֶחֱסָיוּן:
יִרְוְיֻן מִדֶּשֶׁן בֵּיתֶךָ וְנַחַל עֲדָנֶיךָ תַשְׁקֵם:
כִּי עִמְּךָ מְקוֹר חַיִּים, בְּאוֹרְךָ נִרְאֶה־אוֹר:
מְשֹׁךְ חַסְדְּךָ לְיֹדְעֶיךָ וְצִדְקָתְךָ לְיִשְׁרֵי־לֵב:
uncertainties: The first line starts at the margin and the next three are indented, so they are printed as separate verse lines. I kept the line breaks.
There is a comma after חַיִּים in the source.

blocks.text: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁתְּהֵי חֲשׁוּבָה מִצְוַת צִיצִת זוֹ כְּאִלּוּ קִיַּמְתִּיהָ בְּכָל־פְּרָטֶיהָ וְדִקְדּוּקֶיהָ וְכַוָּנוֹתֶיהָ ותרי״ג מִצְוֹת־הַתְּלוּיִם בָּהּ. אָמֵן:
uncertainties: The word at the end of the first line looks like שֶׁתְּהֵי (final yod), not the expected שֶׁתְּהֵא. This needs human verification.
ותרי״ג appears unpointed, with gershayim.
The source has a maqaf in מִצְוֹת־הַתְּלוּיִם. I kept it.
I read the vowel on זוֹ as holam, but it isn't certain.

blocks.text: One then removes the טלית from the face and drapes oneself in such a way that there should be one ציצת in front and one behind on each side.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has sanctified us with His commandments and ordered us to drape ourselves with show-fringes.

How precious is Thy grace, O God, and the children of man shelter in the shadow of Thy wings. They are refreshed by the felicity of Thy house and with the brook of Thy bliss dost Thou water them. For with Thee is the source of life, in Thy light do we behold light. Extend Thy grace to those who acknowledge Thee, and Thy charity to those who are of upright heart.

notes: The page number 1 is printed on both sides of the heading line. There is no separate running head; the section heading sits on the head line.
A full-width horizontal rule separates the Hebrew/rubric section from the English translations at the bottom of the page.
The English below the rule translates only the berakhah and Mah yakar. The page has no English translation for Hineni or Yehi ratzon.

blocks.text: תְּפִלּוֹת.
uncertainties: The letters are printed spaced out (ת פ ל ו ת). Pointing is visible on ת and פ; the full pointing is my best reading.

blocks.text: On entering the Synagogue:

וַאֲנִי בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ אָבֹא בֵיתֶךָ אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה אֶל־הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ:
בְּבֵית אֱלֹהִים נְהַלֵּךְ בְּרָגֶשׁ:
uncertainties: This is set in a large display face. The first verse runs across two lines and the second is a separate indented line.
I read אָבֹא with no vav. I can't tell whether בֵיתֶךָ has a dagesh.

blocks.text: מַה־טֹּבוּ אֹהָלֶיךָ יַעֲקֹב מִשְׁכְּנֹתֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל: וַאֲנִי בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ אָבֹא בֵיתֶךָ אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה אֶל־הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ: יְיָ אָהַבְתִּי מְעוֹן בֵּיתֶךָ וּמְקוֹם מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדֶךָ: וַאֲנִי אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה וְאֶכְרָעָה אֶבְרְכָה לִפְנֵי־יְיָ עֹשִׂי: וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי־לְךָ יְיָ עֵת רָצוֹן אֱלֹהִים בְּרָב־חַסְדֶּךָ עֲנֵנִי בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׁעֶךָ:
uncertainties: The vowel under ר in בְּרָב־חַסְדֶּךָ looks like qamats; I can't tell it from patah at this resolution.
In לִפְנֵי־יְיָ the divine name is set close to the maqaf. I kept the maqaf.

blocks.text: בקשה לר׳ שלמה בן גבירול. ד׳ תנועות ויתד וד׳ תנועות.
uncertainties: The first letter of the first word looks like נ in the scan (נקשה). I read it as בקשה, a likely broken ב, but this needs human verification.
I'm not sure whether the abbreviation mark after לר is a geresh (לר׳) or a yod (לרי).
This is a small unpointed line and is not spoken text. It gives the author and the meter (four vowels, a peg, four vowels).

blocks.text: שַׁחַר אֲבַקֶּשְׁךָ. צוּרִי וּמִשְׂגַּבִּי. אֶעְרוֹךְ לְפָנֶיךָ. שַׁחְרִי וְגַם־עַרְבִּי: לִפְנֵי גְדֻלָּתְךָ. אֶעְמֹד וְאֶבָּהֵל. כִּי־עֵינְךָ תִרְאֶה. כָּל־מַחְשְׁבוֹת לִבִּי: מַה־זֶּה אֲשֶׁר יוּכַל. הַלֵּב וְהַלָּשׁוֹן לַעֲשׂוֹת, וּמַה־כֹּחִי. רוּחִי בְּתוֹךְ קִרְבִּי: הִנֵּה לְךָ תִיטַב. זִמְרַת אֱנוֹשׁ, עַל־כֵּן אוֹדְךָ בְּעוֹד תִּהְיֶה. נִשְׁמַת אֱלוֹהַּ בִּי:
uncertainties: The poem is set as running prose. Periods separate the hemistichs and sof pasuq marks separate the stanzas.
There is a comma after לַעֲשׂוֹת and another after אֱנוֹשׁ, where the pattern would lead you to expect periods. I kept the commas.
I read כֹּחִי (with hiriq yod) in the source.
I'm unsure whether אֶעְמֹד is written with a vav.
I can't confirm the mappiq/dagesh in אֱלוֹהַּ.

blocks.text: Before the morning prayer:

אֲנִי קְרָאתִיךָ כִּי־תַעֲנֵנִי אֵל הַט־אָזְנְךָ לִי שְׁמַע אִמְרָתִי: אֲנִי בְּצֶדֶק אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ אֶשְׂבְּעָה בְהָקִיץ תְּמוּנָתֶךָ: וַאֲנִי עָלֶיךָ בָטַחְתִּי יְיָ אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהַי אָתָּה: שְׁמַע קוֹל תַּחֲנוּנַי בְּשַׁוְּעִי אֵלֶיךָ בְּנָשְׂאִי יָדַי אֶל־דְּבִיר קָדְשֶׁךָ: יְיָ אֱלֹהָי שִׁוַּעְתִּי אֵלֶיךָ וַתִּרְפָּאֵנִי: אֵלֶיךָ יְיָ אֶקְרָא וְאֶל־אֲדֹנָי אֶתְחַנָּן: הָאִירָה פָנֶיךָ עַל־עַבְדֶּךָ הוֹשִׁיעֵנִי בְחַסְדֶּךָ: כִּי־לְךָ יְיָ הוֹחָלְתִּי אַתָּה תַעֲנֶה אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהָי: שְׁמָעָה
uncertainties: This block continues onto s42 (printed page 3), starting with תְפִלָּתִי. The page ends mid-verse after שְׁמָעָה.
The divine name in כִּי־לְךָ יְיָ on the last line has an unusual mark beneath it, possibly a different vowel or a print defect. This needs human verification.
I can't confirm whether פָנֶיךָ / בְהָקִיץ / בָטַחְתִּי / בְחַסְדֶּךָ have a dagesh or not. I read them as rafe per the print.

notes: The running head is תְּפִלּוֹת., with page number 2 on both sides.
A short centered rule separates the Shachar poem from the 'Before the morning prayer' section.

blocks.text: On entering the Synagogue:
And I through the abundance of Thy grace enter Thy house and bow down before Thy holy place in awe of Thee.
In the house of God let us walk in throngs.

How becoming are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel. And I through the abundance of Thy grace enter Thy house and bow down before Thy holy place in awe of Thee. O Lord, I love the site of Thy house, the place of the dwelling of Thy glory. I bow, throw myself down and kneel before the Lord, my Maker. And as for me, my prayer is to Thee, O Lord, at a time of favour. O God, in the abundance of Thy grace respond to me with the truth of Thy salvation.

In the morning I seek Thee, my rock and my fortress. I order my morning and also my evening prayer before Thee. Before Thy grandeur I stand and tremble, for Thine eye sees all the thoughts of my heart. What can heart and tongue accomplish, what can my strength, what can the spirit within me. Behold, man's song pleases Thee. Therefore, I wish to thank Thee as long as God's breath is in me.
Before the morning prayer:

I call to Thee, for Thou dost respond to me, O God, incline Thine ear to me, hear my word. In righteousness may I behold Thy countenance, I am satisfied on waking with Thy likeness. I trust in Thee, O Lord, I say, Thou art my God. Hear the voice of my prayer when I implore Thee, when I raise my hands toward Thine inmost sanctuary. O Lord my God, I implore Thee and Thou healest me. Unto Thee, O Lord, do I call and my Master do I entreat. Let Thy countenance shine upon Thy servant, help me in Thy grace. For I wait for Thee, O Lord, Thou dost respond, O Lord my God.
uncertainties: 'countenance' in the second-to-last sentence is split across lines as 'coun-/tenance' in print. I joined it.
This paragraph continues on s43 (printed page 3) with 'Hear my prayer, O Lord…', but the page break falls at a sentence boundary.

notes: The running head is 'Prayers', with page number 2 on both sides. This is the English facing page for Hebrew page 2 (s40).

There is no English for the Gabirol attribution line.

blocks.text: שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת לְדָוִד שָׂמַחְתִּי בְּאֹמְרִים לִי בֵּית יְיָ נֵלֵךְ: שָׂשׂ אָנֹכִי עַל־אִמְרָתֶךָ כְּמוֹצֵא שָׁלָל רָב: הַקְשִׁיבָה לְקוֹל שַׁוְעִי מַלְכִּי וֵאלֹהָי כִּי־אֵלֶיךָ אֶתְפַּלָּל: יְיָ בֹּקֶר תִּשְׁמַע קוֹלִי בֹּקֶר אֶעֱרָךְ־לְךָ וַאֲצַפֶּה: אֲנִי קְרָאתִיךָ כִּי־תַעֲנֵנִי אֵל הַט־אָזְנְךָ לִי שְׁמַע אִמְרָתִי: רַגְלִי עָמְדָה בְמִישׁוֹר בְּמַקְהֵלִים אֲבָרֵךְ יְיָ:
uncertainties: I can't tell whether בְמִישׁוֹר has a dagesh.
The pointing on אֶעֱרָךְ־לְךָ is my best reading.

blocks.text: שלשה עשר עקרים, בחרוזים מסדורים.
uncertainties: Small unpointed letter-spaced heading. It is spelled מסדורים, with a vav.

blocks.text:
יִגְדַּל אֱלֹהִים חַי וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח נִמְצָא וְאֵין עֵת אֶל־מְצִיאוּתוֹ:
אֶחָד וְאֵין יָחִיד כְּיִחוּדוֹ נֶעְלָם וְגַם אֵין סוֹף לְאַחְדוּתוֹ:
אֵין לוֹ דְּמוּת הַגּוּף וְאֵינוֹ גוּף לֹא נַעֲרוֹךְ אֵלָיו קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ:
קַדְמוֹן לְכָל־דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר נִבְרָא רִאשׁוֹן וְאֵין רֵאשִׁית לְרֵאשִׁיתוֹ:
הִנּוֹ אֲדוֹן עוֹלָם וְכָל־נוֹצָר יוֹרֶה גְדֻלָּתוֹ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ:
שֶׁפַע נְבוּאָתוֹ נְתָנוֹ אֶל אַנְשֵׁי סְגֻלָּתוֹ וְתִפְאַרְתּוֹ:
לֹא קָם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמֹשֶׁה עוֹד נָבִיא וּמַבִּיט אֶת־תְּמוּנָתוֹ:
תּוֹרַת אֱמֶת נָתַן לְעַמּוֹ אֵל עַל־יַד נְבִיאוֹ נֶאֱמַן בֵּיתוֹ:
לֹא יַחֲלִיף הָאֵל וְלֹא יָמִיר דָּתוֹ לְעוֹלָמִים לְזוּלָתוֹ:
צוֹפֶה וְיוֹדֵעַ סְתָרֵינוּ מַבִּיט לְסוֹף דָּבָר בְּקַדְמָתוֹ:
גּוֹמֵל לְאִישׁ חֶסֶד כְּמִפְעָלוֹ נוֹתֵן לְרָשָׁע רָע כְּרִשְׁעָתוֹ:
יִשְׁלַח לְקֵץ יָמִין מְשִׁיחֵנוּ לִפְדּוֹת מְחַכֵּי קֵץ יְשׁוּעָתוֹ:
מֵתִים יְחַיֶּה אֵל בְּרֹב חַסְדּוֹ בָּרוּךְ עֲדֵי־עַד שֵׁם תְּהִלָּתוֹ:
uncertainties: There are 13 printed lines, one per principle. There are no visible separators between hemistichs except spacing.
In line 10, צוֹפֶה וְיוֹדֵעַ is letter-spaced (justification), and the vowel placement is hard to read.

blocks.text: Hear my prayer, O Lord, listen to my entreaty, at my tears do not be silent. Hear, O Lord, and be gracious to me, O Lord, be my aid.

blocks.text: Song of the ascents by David: I am glad when they say to me: Let us go into the House of the Lord. I rejoice at Thy word as one who has found abundant booty. Lister to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to Thee do I pray. O Lord, in the morning listen to my voice, in the morning I address Thee and I have hope. I called to Thee for Thou dost respond to me. O God, incline Thine ear to me, hear my word. My foot has stood on level ground. In assemblies will I praise the Lord.
uncertainties: The source reads 'Lister' (a typo for 'Listen'). I kept it as printed.

blocks.text: The Thirteen Principles
Exalted is the living God and praised. He exists and timeless is His existence.
He is unique and there is nought unique like His uniqueness. He is hidden and infinite too is His unity.
He has not the shape of a body nor is He a body. We cannot estimate His sanctity.
He was there before anything that was created; He is the first and there was no beginning to His beginning.
Behold He is the Master of the world and every creature indicates His grandeur and His rule.
uncertainties: 'creature' is hyphenated across lines in print ('crea-/ture'). I joined it.

blocks.text: The wealth of His prophecy did He bestow upon men of His possession and His glory.
No other prophet arose in Israel like Moses, who perceived His likeness.
The true Torah has God given to His people through His prophet, the faithful one of His house.
God will not alter nor will He change His law for another unto eternity.
He observes and knows our secrets, perceiving even at its beginning the end of a matter.
He treats man kindly according to his conduct and sends disaster to the wicked according to his wickedness.
He will send our Messiah at the end of days to redeem those who wait for the finality of His salvation.
God will revive the dead in the abundance of His grace. Blessed for ever and ever be His renowned Name.
